Now the king of kings Arghun, at the beginning of his reign, made Mas'ud bar Qawti (Bar Qawti?) king in Mosul and all its districts;
and there was great joy for all the Christians.
Yet distress came upon them

on the very day that Arghun came to Ahmad,

Concerning the murder of the Sahib Diwan:
Because the beginning of the dispute between Arghun and Ahmad had been on account of Shams al-Din the Sahib Diwan,
inasmuch as it was said to Arghun,
"The Sahib Diwan poisoned your father."
For this reason, he kept sending envoys and demanding him from Ahmad,
but he would not surrender him to him.
And thus Arghun came to suspect Ahmad
of having consented to the death of the king of kings Abaqa,
in order that he might sit in his place,
and as it [actually happened] {OCR?}.
When Ahmad was defeated {OCR: disguised/put to shame}
and Arghun was victorious,
Shams al-Din fled to the mountains of Media,
and took refuge with the tribe of Kurds who are called Lurs.
Now the chief of the Lurs, whose name was Yusuf Shah,
when he saw that the kingdom was firmly established for Arghun,
came to submit to him,
and he was received gladly,
because he promised to seize the Sahib Diwan and bring him.
And so he went and seized him,
and brought him to Arghun, and presented many gifts.
One hundred myriad (one million) gold dinars were demanded of him as the price of his blood, so that it might not be shed.
And he said:
"If you restore my estates to me,
I am able to give more than this;
otherwise, no."
And the nobles advised him:
"Borrow this amount {OCR?} and present it,
and then they will restore your estates to you."
Therefore, he began to borrow from his kinsmen, his household, his servants, and his friends,
and he collected forty myriad (four hundred thousand).
